**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. History 2 (0560), Paper 2 - Modern World History Since 1870, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2023. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

- Answer FOUR Questions.
- TWO questions must be chosen from SECTION A, ONE from SECTION B and ONE other from SECTION C. One of the two questions chosen from SECTION A must be a Starred question.
- Maps should be used to illustrate answers where appropriate. All questions carry equal marks.

SECTION A: question 1 is compulsory in the sense that the candidate answers either 1A* or 1B* (the two Starred questions) and one other question from the section (2, 3 or 4). SECTION B: answer ONE question (5, 6 or 7). SECTION C: answer ONE question (8, 9 or 10).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

- (a) Bakweri revolt
- (b) Bayang revolt
- (c) Bulu revolt
- (d) Bafut revolt.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Describe briefly the **causes** of any **TWO** of the native resistance to German colonial rule cited below: Bakweri revolt, Bayang revolt, Bulu revolt, Bafut revolt.

[10 marks: 5 for each of the two revolts chosen, causes and effects together being marked 5/5/5/5 in the printed paper]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Between the 1880s and 1914 many Cameroonian peoples resisted German rule by force. The causes were mostly the same everywhere (loss of independence, loss of land and trade, forced labour and taxes, and German violence), but each revolt also had its own causes. Four are given below; a candidate chooses **any two**.

**1. The Bakweri revolt (around Buea, early 1890s).**
- **Defence of independence.** The Bakweri lived on the slopes of Mount Cameroon and refused to accept German authority when the Germans tried to advance from the coast to the mountain, where they wanted a healthy base.
- **Land.** The Germans wanted the rich volcanic soils of the Bakweri for plantations (cocoa, bananas, tobacco and rubber), and the Bakweri feared losing their land.
- **German attempts at control and trade.** The Germans tried to open the roads to the interior and to control local trade, and wanted porters and labourers from the Bakweri.
- **Leaders.** The Bakweri chief Kuva Likenye led the resistance. In 1891 a German expedition under Baron von Gravenreuth was attacked at Buea and Gravenreuth was killed.

**2. The Bayang revolt (Bayang of the Mamfe area of the Cross River basin).**
- **Loss of trade control.** The Bayang, like their neighbours, were traders and middlemen in the trade between the coast and the Cross River region (palm produce, ivory and other goods) and feared that the Germans would break their control.
- **Opposition to German posts and taxes.** The Germans wanted to build posts, to make the people pay taxes and to force them to supply labour and carriers.
- **Defence of independence.** The Bayang were organised in small lineage-based groups without a single king and refused to obey strangers and their appointed chiefs.

**3. The Bulu revolt (south Cameroon forest).**
- **Forced labour and carriers.** The Germans needed Bulu men to carry goods and to build roads, and the Bulu resented it.
- **Taxes and German demands.** The Germans wanted taxes and rubber and ivory from the forest, and punished refusal.
- **Loss of independence.** The Bulu lived in small independent clans and rejected the chiefs imposed by the Germans.

**4. The Bafut revolt (Grassfields).**
- **Defence of the Fon's authority.** The Fon of Bafut ruled a strong and well-organised Grassfields chiefdom and did not want to submit to the Germans.
- **German demands.** The Germans demanded porters, labour and soldiers and tried to control the trade routes through the Grassfields.
- **German expeditions.** From the explorer Eugen Zintgraff (1889-1891) onwards, German expeditions entered the Grassfields to open the road to the north and to impose German authority, and the Bafut resisted these advances.

**Conclusion.** In all these cases the main cause was the same: the Germans were taking away the independence, land, trade and labour of the Cameroonian peoples.
themes: indigenous resistance to german rule in cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Describe briefly the **effects** of any **TWO** of the native resistance to German colonial rule cited below: Bakweri revolt, Bayang revolt, Bulu revolt, Bafut revolt.

[10 marks: 5 for each of the two revolts chosen, causes and effects together being marked 5/5/5/5 in the printed paper]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Each revolt ended in military defeat or submission, but the Germans also learnt that the conquest of the interior would be slow and expensive. A candidate chooses **any two** of the following.

**1. Effects of the Bakweri revolt.**
- The Germans defeated the Bakweri (the main battles were in the early 1890s) and **killed many of them**; their villages were destroyed.
- The Bakweri **lost much of their land** to German plantations (the Germans set up reserves for them and gave the best land to the plantation companies).
- The Bakweri were forced to **work on the plantations** or to carry goods.
- The Germans were able to **establish a strong station at Buea**, which later became the capital of the colony (1901).

**2. Effects of the Bayang revolt.**
- The Germans' **military expeditions** defeated the resistance and **destroyed villages**.
- The Germans were able to **set up an administrative post in the Mamfe area** and to open the Cross River route to the Grassfields.
- The Bayang lost their position as **middlemen** in trade and had to pay taxes and supply labour.
- Chiefs were appointed or recognised by the Germans, and the traditional independence of the clans ended.

**3. Effects of the Bulu revolt.**
- The Germans' **punitive expeditions** killed many people and burnt villages.
- The Bulu were brought under German rule, had to pay taxes, **supply labour and carriers**, and accept **chiefs appointed by the Germans**.
- German stations and trading companies spread into the south and the rubber and ivory trade in the forest increased under German control.
- Missionaries (Presbyterian and Catholic) settled among the Bulu during or after the conquest, and schools were opened.

**4. Effects of the Bafut revolt.**
- The Bafut suffered **losses of men and destruction** in the conflicts and the Fon had to **come to terms** with the Germans.
- The Fon **cooperated** with the Germans afterwards (supplying labourers and carriers) in order to keep his position, and the Germans used Bafut as a base and ally in the Grassfields.
- The Germans were able to **extend their control** towards the Grassfields and the north.
- The Grassfields states lost their independence and had to pay taxes and supply labour.

**Conclusion.** The revolts failed because the Cameroonians fought separately with spears, bows and a few old guns against Germans who had modern rifles and machine guns, but they showed the Cameroonians' wish for independence and prepared later nationalism.
themes: indigenous resistance to german rule in cameroon
